description: To assess cholesterol and triglyceride levels, evaluate heart disease risk, and monitor treatment response

faqs.question: What do high LDL levels mean?
faqs.answer: High LDL (bad cholesterol) levels increase the risk of heart attack and stroke due to plaque build-up in arteries.

faqs.question: What are normal lipid profile values?
faqs.answer: Total cholesterol <200 mg/dL, LDL <100 mg/dL, HDL >40 mg/dL, and triglycerides <150 mg/dL are considered desirable.

faqs.question: Is fasting required for a lipid profile test?
faqs.answer: Yes, 12–14 hours of fasting is required for accurate triglyceride and LDL measurement.

faqs.question: How can I lower my cholesterol naturally?
faqs.answer: Eat more fibre-rich foods, reduce saturated fats, exercise regularly, and avoid smoking and alcohol.

faqs.question: Can I drink water before the lipid profile test?
faqs.answer: Yes, you may drink plain water during the fasting period.

faqs.question: Can I take my regular medication before the test?
faqs.answer: Yes, unless your doctor advises you otherwise. Always inform your healthcare provider about your medicines.

faqs.question: How often should I take a lipid profile test?
faqs.answer: Once every 1–2 years, or more frequently if you have high cholesterol, diabetes, or heart disease.

faqs.question: What causes low HDL levels?
faqs.answer: Smoking, obesity, lack of exercise, and poor diet can lower your HDL (good cholesterol).

faqs.question: Can lipid profile tests be booked online?
faqs.answer: Yes, you can easily book the test through the Metropolis Healthcare website or app.

faqs.question: What happens if my cholesterol is high?
faqs.answer: Your doctor may recommend lifestyle changes, diet modification, or medications to lower your cholesterol.
